the age-dependent function of the thymic epithelial cells and their role in the development of autoimmune diseases.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Sm, Rnp, Ro and La antigens are not only markers for autoimmune diseases but also important parameters for thymus maturation.
the lupus antigenses are not only involved in the regulation of the immune system, but also participate in the control of cell proliferation and differentiation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thymus is an important organ for the development of autoimmune diseases.
the thymus is a major site of Sm and Ro synthesis, and that the concentrations of these antigens are age-dependent.
the lupus antigents are involved in the regulation of thymocyte maturation and differentiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Sm antigen is a marker for the differentiation of thymocytes and that the thymus is the major source of Sm in the body of the rat.
lupus antigents are present in the thymocytes of young animals and decrease during development and ageing.
the thymus is a major source for the production of lupus erythemtosus (LE) antigens.
